Vindoline hybrids 10a and 10i comprising 3,4,5- and 1,4,6-trimethoxyphenyl-substituted chalcone fragments, respectively, displayed substantial activity, featuring IC50 values lower than 0.4 µM on all the investigated cancer cell lines. On the other hand, hybrids 10c–e containing monomethoxy-substituted chalcones, also featuring submicromolar IC50 values on malignant cells, showed moderately lower activities against non-malignant fibroblasts (NIH/3T3), indicating a certain degree of cancer selectivity. The related ferrocene-derived hybrid (10i) and vindoline-free chalcones 14a,b were identified as antiproliferative agents with significantly decreased efficiency, while the ferrocene hybrid comprising an alternative enone sequence in the chalcone residue (11) as well as the zidovudine-derived vindoline hybrid 12 were inactive. Modeling results indicate that the vindoline hybrids bind to the inter-dimer vinca crevice of tubulin oligomers and confirm that the two segments exert a mutually stabilizing effect on the binding of the other, providing a framework for future structure optimization.
items.authors: Etelka Ferenczi, Dóra K. Menyhárd, Adriána Kovács, Ágnes Gömöry, László Drahos, Péter Keglevich

items.title: Tree Felling by Chainsaw: A Laboratory Assessment of the Hinge Flexibility in Relation to Its Width and to the Back-Cut Height
items.abstract: Motor-manual tree felling by chainsaws remains a widespread but hazardous forestry practice. This operation consists of executing a directional notch followed by a felling cut that releases a hinge. The hinge geometry (defined by its height, width, and alignment relative to the directional notch) is a critical determinant of safe felling, controlling the direction and stability of the falling tree. How the hinge's geometry might affect these aspects has not yet been studied. This study evaluates variations in hinge flexibility and bending stiffness using wooden square beams of European beech (Fagus sylvatica) and silver fir (Abies alba) in a rig reproducing the classical felling cuts, varying hinge geometry combinations. Two geometric parameters, back-cut height (S) and hinge width (C) were examined. Mechanical testing was performed using a universal testing machine, and load–deformation curves were smoothed with a Savitzky–Golay filter; the Critical Bending Angle and Yield Point were determined by using the 0.02° offset method and absorbed energy by Simpson integration. Results reveal different mechanical behavior between the two dimensions: hinge width primarily determines yield force, whereas back-cut height governs flexibility, showing a strong negative correlation with the critical bending angle. Significant species-specific differences were observed for both response variables. Hinge toughness, expressed as absorbed energy per unit hinge cross-section, was found to be independent of back-cut height and about 1.8 times higher in beech (0.39 kJ·m⁻²) than in fir (0.22 kJ·m⁻²).
items.authors: Cristiano Foderi, Francesco Neri, Fabio Fabiano, Simone Calamai, Andrea Laschi, Marco Togni

items.title: Integrated Electrical Resistivity Tomography and Borehole Correlation for Characterizing Salt Formation Geometry and Groundwater Circulation at Slănic Prahova, Romania
items.abstract: Salt (halite) massifs undergoing active dissolution are among the most hazard-prone geological settings for ground instability, and their monitoring requires a reliable geometric model of the salt body and its overburden. This study presents an integrated geoelectrical–geological characterization of the salt formation at Slănic Prahova (Romania), carried out in 2026 within the GEOMONITOR project. Six electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) profiles were acquired along three transects, each surveyed with both Wenner and Schlumberger electrode configurations (5 m electrode spacing), and correlated with lithological logs from three boreholes (F1, F2, F3) that intercepted the salt formation at 98.0 m, 44.1 m and 68.0 m below ground, corresponding to 301.0, 346.4 and 327.0 m a.s.l. respectively. Reading both datasets in absolute elevation is the key step of the workflow: it shows that the salt roof enters the imaged volume only in the Baia Roșie sector, where a body exceeding 1000 Ω·m occupies the 348–370 m a.s.l. interval—an elevation range that agrees, to within the ±15 m datum uncertainty of the sections, with the shallowest salt roof recorded by drilling (346.4 m a.s.l.)—whereas along the other two transects, the salt roof lies 35–80 m below the base of the inverted models. The sections delineate a strongly heterogeneous cover, predominantly conductive (1–10 Ω·m) and punctuated by transition zones with steep lateral resistivity gradients. Two consequences follow for hazard-oriented surveys of this kind: shallow resistive anomalies confined to the uppermost meters cannot be attributed to the salt roof, and the absence of a resistive anomaly along a line of this length is not evidence for the absence of salt. The conductive–resistive contact zones, rather than the resistive cores themselves, are identified as the priority targets for hydrogeological monitoring, since they can concentrate permeability contrasts and control dissolution. The survey is a single, non-repeated campaign without pore-fluid characterization, and is therefore presented as the baseline from which a monitoring network can be designed rather than as a record of temporal change. The elevation-based reconciliation of ERT and borehole data proposed here is transferable to other salt karst settings.
items.authors: Liliana Irina Stoian, Anca Margareta Isac, Violeta Monica Radu, Valentina Maria Cetean, Elena Aurelia Tudor, Antonio Ulmeanu

items.title: Effectiveness of the 23-Valent Pneumococcal Polysaccharide Vaccine in Reducing Mortality Among Older Adults: A Real-World Retrospective Cohort Study in Guangzhou, China
items.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the real-world effectiveness of the 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) in reducing all-cause, pneumonia-related, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)-related mortality in adults aged ≥60 years. Methods: In this retrospective cohort study using existing health surveillance data, individuals aged ≥60 years on 1 January 2020 were followed until 31 August 2025 and classified by PPSV23 vaccination status. Propensity score matching (PSM) at a 1:1 ratio balanced sex, age, regional distribution, urbanization level and influenza vaccination status. Time-dependent Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HR) and vaccine effectiveness (VE), defined as (1 − HR) × 100%. Subgroup, negative control (mortality from traffic accidents), and E-value sensitivity analyses were performed. Results: After PSM, 453,500 individuals were included, with a mean follow-up of 5.61 years. All-cause mortality was 3.93 per 1000 person-years in vaccinated versus 9.57 in unvaccinated individuals. PPSV23 vaccination reduced all-cause mortality (VE = 43.1%, 95% CI: 41.2–45.0%), pneumonia-related mortality (VE = 46.2%, 95% CI: 39.6–52.1%), and COPD-related mortality (VE = 33.5%, 95% CI: 20.9–44.2%) (all p 0.001). In a cause-specific decomposition, pneumonia- and COPD-related deaths together explained only 14.9% of the absolute reduction in all-cause deaths, whereas circulatory diseases and malignant tumors accounted for 36.8% and 31.9%, respectively. Among those also vaccinated against influenza, VE was 48.0% and 38.2% for pneumonia- and COPD-related mortality, respectively. For COPD-related mortality, the benefit was greater in men (VE = 42.3%) and in those aged ≥70 years (70–79 years, VE = 45.6%; ≥80 years, VE = 52.0%). PPSV23 was not associated with the negative control outcome (p = 0.247); E-values (1.98–2.44) indicated robustness to unmeasured confounding. Conclusions: PPSV23 vaccination was associated with significantly lower all-cause, pneumonia-related, and COPD-related mortality among elderly individuals aged ≥60 years. However, the observed association with all-cause mortality should be interpreted cautiously. Continued promotion of PPSV23 vaccination and advocacy for combined influenza–pneumococcal vaccination strategies are recommended.
items.authors: Yan Kang, Zhiwei Zheng, Juan Qi, Lin Tang, Wen Wang, Xinqi Lin

items.title: Next-Generation Modulation and Control of Power Electronic Systems: AI-Enabled Control, Digital Twins, Fault-Tolerant Operation, and Cyber-Physical Security
items.abstract: Power electronic systems are evolving from conventional fixed-function converters toward intelligent, adaptive, and cyber-physical energy-conversion platforms in which modulation, predictive control, artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins (DTs), fault diagnosis, and cybersecurity increasingly interact within a unified closed-loop architecture. This paper presents an integrated review and mathematical framework for next-generation modulation and control of power electronic systems, with an emphasis on advanced modulation, predictive control, AI-assisted adaptation, converter-oriented digital state estimation, fault-tolerant operation, and cyber-resilient control. The proposed framework links converter dynamics, state and parameter estimation, physical faults, cyber disturbances, supervisory anomaly assessment, and mode-dependent control reconfiguration. Two clearly separated validation levels complement the literature synthesis: experimentally measured operating data are used to establish physically representative operating conditions, whereas a dedicated converter-control model is used to evaluate closed-loop dynamic resilience. Under a combined physical/cyber disturbance, resilient reconfiguration reduced the post-event speed RMSE from 9.203 to 0.425 rad/s, the peak speed error from 29.999 to 1.724 rad/s, and the maximum current from 69.112 to 10.662 A, while eliminating 829 current-constraint violations observed without resilience. Across 100 randomized Monte Carlo trials, the mean post-event RMSE decreased from 11.951 ± 3.060 to 0.769 ± 0.291 rad/s, with the corresponding 95% confidence interval narrowing from 11.351–12.550 to 0.712–0.826 rad/s. The results provide simulation-based, closed-loop evidence that coordinated state estimation, anomaly assessment, and resilient reconfiguration can substantially limit disturbance propagation while maintaining converter-control performance under combined physical and cyber abnormalities. Hardware-in-the-loop and embedded real-time implementation remain subjects for future validation.
items.authors: Somayeh Soroush, Samir Abood, Annamalai Annamalai, Mohamed Chouikha, Turki Nejress

items.title: Emotion Regulation and Brain Mechanisms: A Transdiagnostic Perspective on Neural Circuits, Individual Differences, and Clinical Translation
items.abstract: Emotion regulation (ER) difficulties are now firmly established as a transdiagnostic feature of psychiatric and stress-related disorders. Large-scale meta-analyses published in 2026 confirmed ER impairments across fifteen diagnostic categories, shifting the key question from whether ER is transdiagnostic to how this knowledge can inform diagnosis and treatment. This Perspective argues that ER should be conceptualized as a transdiagnostic neurocognitive dimension rather than a disorder-specific deficit. To support this view, three complementary studies are integrated: neuroimaging studies of prefrontal-limbic and large-scale brain networks involved in cognitive reappraisal; evidence of ER-related neural alterations across mood, anxiety, trauma-related, personality, and addictive disorders; and research on individual differences and neuromodulation that explain variability in regulatory capacity and treatment response. ER is framed within a broader executive-function model, operating as a “hot” executive process alongside “cool” cognitive-control functions. Building on this evidence, a Layered Transdiagnostic Model of Emotion Regulation (LTM-ER) is proposed. The model includes a shared transdiagnostic core circuit (Layer 1), disorder-specific neural signatures (Layer 2), and individual moderators such as developmental history, dispositional traits, regulatory strategies, and stimulation parameters (Layer 3). Five testable predictions are derived from the model, highlighting how multimodal biomarkers and personalized interventions may advance precision approaches to emotion dysregulation across psychiatric disorders.
items.authors: Sandra Carvalho

items.title: Modulational-Stability Topology and Symmetric Instability Spectra in Non-Maxwellian Heavy Ion-Acoustic Plasmas: Akhmediev Breathers and Higher-Order Rogue Waves
items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analytical and numerical investigation of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation derived from the heavy ion-acoustic wave (HIAW) model, which governs the evolution of weakly nonlinear wave packets and their chaotic envelope dynamics. The modulational instability (MI), symmetric instability spectra, multi-breathing solitons, and rogue waves associated with modified Cairns–Tsallis distributed particles have yet to be investigated. The derived evolution equation establishes onset criteria, which distinguish between the dark and bright solitons in two distinct regimes. For the considered heavy ion-acoustic plasma, separate sign analyses of dispersion and nonlinear coefficients in the carrier wavenumber-temperature ratio (k,β)-plane reveal alternating or multiple stability–instability regions that are separated by an intermediate unstable domain and are independently confirmed by the nonsingular P/Q contours. The analytical stability criteria are further validated through one-dimensional stability profiles and contour maps, which consistently reproduce the predicted disconnected stability structure and identify the unstable region supporting bell-shaped bright envelope solitons. We further demonstrate that the plasma parameters produce the qualitatively distinct transitions in both the MI threshold and growth rate bandwidth under different temperature-ratio (β-values), which reveal a nontrivial control mechanism for nonlinear wave localization. The Darboux transformation is used to generate exact Akhmediev breather solutions, which produce rich families of multi-breathing wave patterns. The robustness of the theoretical framework is confirmed by a split-step Fourier method that exhibits an excellent numerical verification of the Akhmediev breather solution. Our findings identify a new class of stability transitions and breather dynamics in nonlinear dispersive media, providing analytical insights into wave localization and super freak wave phenomena governed by a nonlinear Schrödinger equation.
items.authors: Abdullah Khan, Amal Alabdullatif, Yanfang Ji, Guangrui Yao

items.title: Human Development, Industrialization, Renewable Energy, and Environmental Taxation as Determinants of CO2 Emissions: Evidence from Heterogeneous Panel and Quantile Analysis
items.abstract: Carbon dioxide emissions remain the principal driver of anthropogenic climate change, yet the socioeconomic forces that shape per capita emissions differ markedly across the distribution of emitting economies. This study examines the determinants of carbon dioxide emissions per capita using a balanced structure of 1189 country–year observations drawn from a panel of 41 countries over the period 1995–2023. Four explanatory variables are considered: the Human Development Index, the share of manufacturing value added in gross domestic product, the share of primary energy sourced from renewables, and environmentally related tax revenue expressed as a percentage of gross domestic product. Cross-sectional dependence and slope heterogeneity are formally tested and confirmed, motivating the use of second-generation panel techniques throughout. The Pesaran cross-sectionally augmented Dickey–Fuller test reveals a mixed order of integration, and the Westerlund error-correction-based cointegration test confirms a long-run equilibrium relationship among the series. Long-run marginal effects estimated through the Common Correlated Effects Mean Group and Augmented Mean Group estimators show that human development, manufacturing intensity, and environmentally related tax revenue raise per capita emissions on average, while renewable energy penetration lowers them. Method of Moments Quantile Regression uncovers substantial distributional heterogeneity: the manufacturing effect changes across the conditional distribution, shifting from emission-enhancing at lower quantiles to emission-reducing above the median. Human development and environmentally related tax revenue remain positively associated with emissions, although their effects weaken at higher emission levels. By contrast, the mitigating influence of renewable energy is stable across all quantiles. Dumitrescu–Hurlin causality results indicate bidirectional relationships between emissions and all covariates, with the feedback effect from emissions to human development representing the weakest causal linkage. The findings qualify simple average-based policy prescriptions and support differentiated, distribution-sensitive climate and fiscal policy design.
items.authors: Sukhrob Kholmatov, Nodir Jumaev, Nuriddin Shanyazov, Kamola Kilicheva, Abdurakhmon Abdukhamidov, Zokir Mamadiyarov

items.title: A Semantic-Gated Structural Diversity Penalty to Mitigate Orchestrated Recommendation Attacks in the SIoT
items.abstract: The Social Internet of Things (SIoT) trust algorithms typically assume peer recommendations are independent, this leaves them vulnerable to coordinated Fake Relationship Attacks (FRA). Adversaries exploit this vulnerability by creating dense malicious cliques to manipulate trust calculations and bypass standard anomaly thresholds. In an effort to eliminate this issue without disrupting legitimate consensus, this paper proposes a Semantic-Gated Structural Diversity Penalty based on localized neighborhood partitioning. The defense operates purely on the edge and is able to extract connected components from the recommendation subgraph, separating the coordinated topological islands. The framework acts as a multi-stage logic gate to neutralize Sybil cliques executing trust inflation or synchronized bad-mouthing, while protecting the legitimate collaborative communities. An exponential discounting factor is applied exclusively to synchronized malicious cliques, preserving the trust weights of honest nodes. Experimental results across escalating attack volumes, adaptive jitter, and node mobility scenarios demonstrate that our mechanism systematically suppresses trust manipulation. The framework sustains accurate node classification with high resilience (demonstrating an empirical F1-Score of 0.986 and a False Positive Rate of 0.006), achieving security convergence at a lightweight O(k2) edge complexity. This approach provides robust protection against orchestrated collusion without requiring heavy cryptographic validation or intensive machine-learning-based trust estimation.
items.authors: Mohcine Baalla, Driss Bouzidi

items.title: Seasonal and Interannual Variability of Coastal Black Sea Waters off Bulgaria (2022–2025): A Copernicus Marine Reanalysis Assessment
items.abstract: This study assessed spatial, seasonal, and interannual variability in physical and biogeochemical indicators in surface waters along the Bulgarian Black Sea coast during 2022–2025 to provide an integrated characterization of coastal marine conditions. Copernicus Marine Level 4 multiyear reanalysis products at 0.025° × 0.025° resolution were aggregated into four climatological seasons and summarized for a 25 km coastal strip divided at Cape Emine into northern and southern sectors. Sea-water potential temperature increased from a four-year winter mean of 9.02 °C to 24.70 °C in summer, with the southern sector warmer in all 16 season–year comparisons. Salinity peaked in winter (18.276 × 10−3) and was lowest in summer (17.684 × 10−3), with consistently higher values in the south. Current-vector magnitude was highest in summer (0.0614 m s−1), without persistent sectoral predominance. Chlorophyll-a, net primary production, phytoplankton carbon biomass, and dissolved molecular oxygen peaked in spring and were consistently higher in the northern sector; nitrate was also higher there in 15 of 16 comparisons. Biological productivity peaked in spring 2024, while 2025 showed lower biological indicators than 2022 across all season–sector combinations. The four-year series does not support long-term trend inference but provides a reproducible framework for integrated coastal assessment.
items.authors: Georgi Belev, Petja Ivanova-Radovanova, Kalina Tilko, Donka Shopova-Kozhuharova, Kristiyan Panayotov, Velimira Stoyanova

items.title: A Layered Decision-Aware Forecasting Architecture for Noisy Panel Environments
items.abstract: Machine learning forecasting systems in noisy, non-stationary, multi-entity environments are commonly optimized for pointwise predictive accuracy, although many downstream decisions depend on the relative ordering of entities rather than exact numerical forecasts. This creates a potential prediction–ranking–decision misalignment, where the model with the lowest forecast error may not generate the most useful ranking or decision outcome. This paper proposes a Layered Decision-Aware Forecasting Architecture (LDFA) that separates predictive calibration from decision-oriented transformation. Layers 1 and 2 generate heterogeneous forecasts through base learners, stacking, and adaptive weighting, while the main methodological contribution is Layer 3: a selective post-prediction controller based on source selection, activation gating, veto logic, and regime-aware scaling. LDFA is evaluated using daily data for 30 EGX firms from 2020 to 2025 under a leakage-controlled expanding-window walk-forward protocol. The results show that prediction, ranking, and decision metrics favor different models: the Ridge meta-model provides the strongest target-scale accuracy, the XGBRankerLTR learning-to-rank baseline achieves the strongest ranking information coefficient (IC), and the SoftmaxHybridGate achieves the highest Sharpe ratio. The Layer 3 controller slightly improves over the Ridge backbone in mean daily IC, Sharpe ratio, and maximum drawdown, but the gains are modest and not statistically conclusive. Ablation and sensitivity analyses show that uncontrolled correction is harmful, while selective activation is the main value-adding mechanism. Transaction-cost, dynamic-controller, bootstrap, and top-k robustness tests further indicate that LDFA is most useful under selective decision settings rather than as a universally dominant model. The findings position LDFA as a transparent decision-aware forecasting architecture for studying and managing prediction–ranking–decision trade-offs in noisy panel environments.
items.authors: Mohamed Sameh Hassanein, Reham Nasser Farag, Samar Turki, Osama Emam

items.title: Capillin, a Polyacetylene from Argyranthemum frutescens, a Promising Hit Compound for Antikinetoplastid Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Chagas disease and leishmaniasis, caused by the protozoan Trypanosoma cruzi and different Leishmania species, respectively, remain public health problems in developing regions due to high prevalence and the limited efficacy and safety of current treatments. Plant-derived natural products are emerging as a promising source of safer antikinetoplastid agents. The present work explores Argyranthemum frutescens as a source of antiparasitic compounds to identify new therapeutic candidates. To address this aim, a bioassay-guided fractionation of the ethanolic root extract from cultivated A. frutescens was carried out against kinetoplastids, including T. cruzi, L. amazonensis, and L. donovani. Polyacetylenes with leishmanicidal and trypanocidal activity were identified using this approach. Among them, compound 1 showed greater activity than the reference drug miltefosine against L. amazonensis and T. cruzi. Compound 1 showed activity against the amastigote stages of both parasites, surpassing the activity of the leishmanicidal reference drug. Notably, compound 1 showed a good selectivity index against the mammalian cell line. The findings indicated that the nature of the chemical group present at the propargyl–benzyl position plays a role in compound bioactivity. Subsequent assays revealed that this compound induces programmed cell death-related processes in T. cruzi and L. amazonensis, including ATP depletion, chromatin condensation, plasma membrane damage, accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and alterations in mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm). Collectively, these findings highlight the potential of polyacetylenes as promising antikinetoplastid lead compounds and identify A. frutescens as a valuable natural source for the development of therapeutic agents against Chagas disease and leishmaniasis.
items.authors: Suhib Muhsen Hasan Al-Dalaeen, Carlos J. Bethencourt-Estrella, Ines Sifaoui, Atteneri López-Arencibia, María González-Linares, Isabel L. Bazzocchi

items.title: The Mediating Role of Resilience in the Association Between Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms Among College Students at a Hispanic-Serving Institution in a U.S.–Mexico Border Region
items.abstract: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are prevalent concerns among college students, yet less is known about the role of resilience in their association among students in U.S.–Mexico border regions. This cross-sectional study examined whether resilience statistically mediated the association between anxiety and depressive symptoms while controlling for sociodemographic factors and year of data collection. Participants were a convenience sample of 857 college students attending a Hispanic-serving institution in a U.S.–Mexico border region from 2021 to 2025. Anxiety, resilience, and depressive symptoms were measured using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, Brief Resilience Scale, and Patient Health Questionnaire-9, respectively. Mediation analysis was conducted using PROCESS Model 4 with 5000 bootstrap samples. Higher anxiety was associated with lower resilience (B = −0.056, p 0.001), and greater resilience was associated with lower depressive symptoms (B = −1.379, p 0.001). The indirect association of anxiety with depressive symptoms through resilience was significant (B = 0.077, 95% bootstrap CI [0.052, 0.103]). The direct association remained significant (B = 0.700, p 0.001), indicating partial statistical mediation. These findings suggest that resilience is an important factor in the association between anxiety and depressive symptoms and may inform comprehensive student mental health initiatives.
items.authors: Marivic B. Torregosa, Orlando M. Patricio

items.title: Advances in Semen Extenders for Small Ruminant Sperm Preservation: Biological Mechanisms and Emerging Strategies
items.abstract: Semen preservation represents a fundamental component of reproductive biotechnology in small ruminants, supporting artificial insemination programs, genetic improvement, germplasm conservation, and sustainable livestock production. However, ram and buck spermatozoa are highly susceptible to cryoinjury induced by cold shock, oxidative stress, osmotic imbalance, and membrane destabilization during cooling, freezing, and thawing procedures. Consequently, semen extenders play a critical role in maintaining sperm viability, motility, membrane integrity, mitochondrial activity, and fertilizing capacity during preservation. This narrative review summarizes the biological basis of sperm preservation in sheep and goats and discusses the principal conventional and emerging extender systems used in small ruminant semen cryopreservation. Conventional extender components, including buffering systems, energy substrates, cryoprotective agents, egg yolk, and milk proteins, are reviewed with emphasis on their mechanisms of action and protective effects against cryodamage. Particular attention is given to species-specific limitations associated with buck seminal plasma enzymes and their interactions with egg yolk- and milk-based extenders. In addition, recent advances involving chemically defined extenders, soy lecithin formulations, antioxidants, synthetic membrane stabilizers, and nanotechnology-derived additives are discussed as promising alternatives aimed at improving cryosurvival, reducing oxidative stress, and enhancing extender standardization and biosafety. Practical applications of semen extenders in artificial insemination and semen banking are also discussed together with current methodological limitations, species-specific challenges, and future research priorities. Although numerous emerging strategies have demonstrated promising improvements in laboratory sperm-quality parameters, evidence supporting consistent fertility benefits under field conditions remains limited. Overall, this review critically evaluates current knowledge and highlights the need for species-specific, protocol-oriented, and well-standardized approaches to advance semen preservation in small ruminants.
items.authors: Daniel Berean, Liviu Marian Bogdan, Ionela Ut, Raluca Cimpean

items.title: From Rhetoric to Practice: Governance Pathways for Green Infrastructure in Ghana, with Lessons from African and U.S. Tropical Coastal Cities
items.abstract: Urban flooding persists in Ghana’s rapidly urbanizing cities. Although green infrastructure (GI) is recognized in national and metropolitan policy as a complement to conventional drainage, its translation into financed, owned, maintained and monitored infrastructure remains uneven. Using structured qualitative document analysis and focused cross-case synthesis, this study compares Ghana with Dar es Salaam, Durban, Dakar, Honolulu, Miami–Dade, New Orleans and Houston. A central documentary finding is a custodianship mismatch. The reviewed instruments identify strategic coordination, sectoral authority and selected O M responsibilities but do not consistently articulate their connection to budgeting, asset ownership, routine O M and performance accountability. The comparator cases provide context-dependent lessons on participation, institutionalization, mandate alignment and usable guidance, while distinguishing adaptable governance principles from capacity-dependent preconditions. The paper contributes a Barrier → Lever → Stage → Output framework that begins by connecting existing mandates and establishing ownership, finance, O M and equity safeguards for accountable pilots before conditional integration and scaling. The framework and its four associated relationships are presented as testable propositions rather than a validated implementation model.
items.authors: Selorm Abla Afeke, Brian Deal

items.title: Ca sub 4 /sub Mab-3: A Novel Anti-Human Cadherin-4/R-Cadherin Monoclonal Antibody
items.abstract: Cadherin-4 (CDH4/R-cadherin) is a type I cadherin involved in diverse processes of neural development and cancer. Although several anti-CDH4 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) have been established for Western blotting, mAbs suitable for flow cytometric analysis of CDH4 have not been described. To generate anti-CDH4 mAbs for flow cytometry, we used a flow cytometry-based high-throughput screening strategy. Among the generated mAbs, Ca4Mab-3 (IgG1, κ) selectively recognized CDH4-overexpressed Chinese hamster ovary-K1 (CHO/CDH4) cells by flow cytometry and showed no detectable cross-reactivity with 21 other CDHs, including both type I and type II CDHs. Ca4Mab-3 also detected endogenous CDH4 in human breast cancer (MDA-MB-231) and osteosarcoma (U2OS) cell lines. The apparent dissociation constants (KD) of Ca4Mab-3 for CHO/CDH4 and U2OS cells were 1.4 × 10⁻⁹ M and 1.1 × 10⁻⁹ M, respectively. In addition, Ca4Mab-3 successfully detected endogenous CDH4 in Western blotting. These results indicate that Ca4Mab-3 is a highly specific anti-CDH4 mAb that can be used in flow cytometry and Western blotting. Ca4Mab-3 may serve as a useful tool for investigating CDH4 function and may have potential applications in the development of therapeutic strategies for CDH4-positive tumors.
items.authors: Kaito Suzuki, Tomohiro Tanaka, Mika K. Kaneko, Hiroyuki Suzuki, Yukinari Kato

items.title: The Human Labial Superficial Musculoaponeurotic System (SMAS): Anatomy, Imaging, and Biomechanical and Sensory Implications—A Narrative Review
items.abstract: The superficial musculoaponeurotic system (SMAS) is a fundamental concept in facial anatomy and surgery, but its organization within the human lips remains incompletely defined. This narrative review critically reassesses the anatomical evidence for a labial SMAS and its regional configuration. Published anatomical, histological, and imaging evidence was critically reviewed. The literature review is complemented by original qualitative histological and imaging observations of the human lips, included exclusively for morphological correlation with the published anatomical evidence and not as an independent quantitative study. The available evidence does not demonstrate a classical, readily separable laminar SMAS within the lips. Instead, it supports a three-dimensional connective tissue network extending from the oral mucosa to the skin and intimately incorporating the orbicularis oris muscle. This organization is associated with neurovascular structures and may have biomechanical and sensory implications, although these functional interpretations are not directly demonstrated by the present material. The labial connective tissue architecture differs from the classical laminar SMAS described in other facial regions and may represent its regional equivalent. Further three-dimensional anatomical studies are required to establish this interpretation conclusively. By defining the normal fibromuscular architecture of the lips and the limits of its visualization, this review provides an anatomical framework for interpreting lip imaging while emphasizing that a labial SMAS is not currently a validated diagnostic or prognostic marker.
items.authors: José Martín-Cruces, Estefanía del Rocío Ocampo Poma, Luis Alberto Chauca Bajaña, Mirian Teulé-Trull, Patricia Cuendias, Yolanda García-Mesa

items.title: Pre-Analytical Errors Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Multi-Year Retrospective Observational Study
items.abstract: Objective: The pre-analytical phase is the stage at which laboratory errors most frequently occur and is therefore of critical importance for patient safety. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the marked increase in workload, organizational restructuring, staff and resource redeployment, changes in patient volume and clinical workflows, and disease-related pathophysiological alterations affecting specimen characteristics created unprecedented conditions that could influence laboratory quality indicators. This study aimed to characterize changes in specimen rejection rates across the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and normalization periods between 2018 and 2023, and to determine whether pandemic-related disruptions in health care delivery were associated with differences in the number, rate, and distribution of specimen rejections according to clinical unit, rejection reason, and time interval, with emphasis on the magnitude of these differences rather than statistical significance alone. The study also sought to generate evidence that could inform the development of preventive systems and strengthen laboratory preparedness for future large-scale disruptions to health care services. Materials and Methods: This retrospective observational study used routinely collected, aggregated laboratory information system (LIS) data from the Central Laboratory of Istanbul Atlas University Hospital for 1 January 2018 through 31 December 2023. The LIS extract was restricted to eligible specimen types, including spot and 24 h urine, serum, and whole-blood or plasma specimens collected in EDTA-, citrate-, or heparin-containing tubes; all other specimen types were excluded. Specimen rejection rates were evaluated by study period, clinical unit, time interval, and rejection reason. For cross-period comparisons, the total number of specimens within each respective study period was used as the denominator for calculating rejection rates, whereas for rejection-reason-specific analyses, the number of specimen types relevant to each rejection category was used as the denominator. Negative-binomial regression with denominator-based offsets estimated adjusted rejection-rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with Bonferroni adjustment for selected pairwise comparisons. No missing or unclassifiable values were identified; no imputation was required. Reporting follows STROBE and the RECORD extension for studies using routinely collected health data. Results: The overall rejection rate increased progressively from 0.23% in the pre-pandemic period to 0.49% during the pandemic and 0.65% in the normalization period, and monthly observed rates supported this progressive increase. In adjusted terms, the rejection rate was 2.20-fold higher during the pandemic than in the pre-pandemic period (95% CI: 1.96–2.46) and increased a further 1.42-fold in the normalization period compared with the pandemic period (95% CI: 1.27–1.59). Across clinical units, the emergency department had the highest observed rejection rate, whereas intensive care units showed the highest adjusted rejection rates during the pandemic (RR = 1.34 versus the emergency department, 95% CI: 1.00–1.80) and normalization periods. Hemolysis and clotting were the dominant rejection reasons; although clotting had the highest observed rates in the pre-pandemic and pandemic periods, hemolysis ranked highest after adjustment in all periods and separated significantly from clotting only in the normalization period (RR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.65–2.35). Time-interval effects were context-dependent rather than uniform and became informative mainly in combination with clinical unit or rejection reason: intensive care unit rejections peaked in the daytime interval during the pandemic (RR = 1.84 versus the evening interval, 95% CI: 1.06–3.19), and in the normalization period emergency department–hemolysis emerged as the leading adjusted clinical unit–rejection reason combination (RR = 1.89 versus intensive care unit–hemolysis, 95% CI: 1.19–3.00), while clotting remained centered on intensive care units and became more concentrated in the overnight and early-morning interval. Conclusions: Pre-analytical specimen rejection increased progressively across the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and normalization periods, with adjusted effect sizes indicating a substantial and sustained deterioration rather than a transient pandemic-related disturbance, and with persistent differences in rejection patterns according to clinical unit, time interval, and rejection reason. The further increase observed in the normalization period suggests that pandemic-related disruptions were associated with sustained changes in pre-analytical performance but were unlikely to be the sole explanation. Emergency department–hemolysis during the normalization period and intensive care unit–related clotting emerged as the most concrete quality-monitoring targets. Integrating rejection rates and counts with stratified monitoring by clinical unit, time interval, and rejection reason in combination may support earlier identification of emerging risks, more targeted preventive interventions, and stronger laboratory preparedness for future large-scale disruptions to health care services.
items.authors: Betül Özbek Kurtul, Bağnu Dündar, Fatma Bozkurt, Sevgi Koçyiğit Sevinç, Çiğdem Aktaş, Asiye Gök Yurttaş

items.title: The Stability and Response Boundaries of AVOC-BVOC Dominance Under Extreme Anthropogenic Emission Reductions: A Natural Experiment in Sichuan, China
items.abstract: Regional volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions arise from both anthropogenic volatile organic compounds (AVOCs) and biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs), yet the stability of their relative dominance under extreme anthropogenic emission reductions and the spatial extent of potential shifts remain unclear. Using the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown as a natural experiment, we developed a unified 3 km monthly AVOC-BVOC emission inventory for Sichuan Province. The lockdown substantially reduced AVOC emissions but did not eliminate a persistent AVOC emission baseline. Industrial sources consistently contributed approximately 73% of AVOCs, even during the strict lockdown. Continuous production industries accounted for 62.4% of industrial process emissions. Meanwhile, regional VOC emissions remained strongly dominated by BVOCs, which accounted for 92.43% of annual emissions. Despite this strong anthropogenic perturbation, 82.99% of grid cells retained their original dominant source type. Source shifts occurred in only 17.01% of grid cells. These shifts were concentrated in basin margin transition zones, where AVOC and BVOC contributions were comparable. This spatial pattern indicates that extreme anthropogenic emission reductions primarily altered AVOC emission intensity rather than regional source dominance. Persistent industrial emissions maintained a stable anthropogenic emission baseline. In contrast, the stable BVOC background constrained the spatial extent of source shifts. Together, these constraints confined source dominance changes to sensitive transition zones and defined a clear spatial response boundary. These findings reveal the structural and spatial constraints on regional VOC responses to anthropogenic emission reductions and provide a scientific basis for spatially differentiated VOC control in regions with complex terrain.
items.authors: Shiao Xu, Lin Yi, Qi Zhang, Xinyi Wang, Feng Duan

items.title: Serum Melatonin at Admission and Discharge in Schizophrenia: A Prospective Longitudinal Controlled Study
items.abstract: Schizophrenia is associated with circadian and neuroendocrine disturbances, but whether circulating melatonin changes with acute clinical state remains uncertain. This prospective longitudinal controlled study measured serum melatonin at 12:00 and 00:00 in 43 hospitalized patients after admission and before discharge, and during one session in 42 healthy controls. Psychopathology was assessed using the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS). Nonparametric comparisons used family-specific Holm adjustment; exploratory correlations used false-discovery-rate control. In comparisons without covariate adjustment, midday concentrations were higher in patients at admission and discharge (Holm p = 0.013 and 0.007), but the differences did not remain significant after Holm correction in exploratory models adjusted for BMI, age, and sex (29 patients and 40 controls). Median within-patient changes were −0.14 pg/mL at 12:00 (95% CI −0.27 to 0.74) and 0.00 pg./mL at 00:00 (95% CI −2.00 to 6.35); both Holm p = 1.000. Total PANSS decreased by a median of 14 points among 24 complete pairs. No change-PANSS correlation survived multiplicity correction. Two daily samples demonstrate a midday–midnight concentration difference but cannot characterize circadian phase, amplitude, or total secretion. No short-term melatonin change was detected during hospitalization; this does not establish equivalence or confirm or exclude trait-biomarker status. State-marker utility remains uncertain, and patient–control differences may reflect medication, smoking, or confounding by assay plate.
items.authors: Armando Luis Morera-Fumero, Estefanía Diaz-Mesa, Silvia Yelmo-Cruz, Pedro Abreu-González, María Lourdes Fernández-López

items.title: A Sustainable Vibration Isolation Technique Using Half-Filled Trenches with Sand–Crumb Rubber Mixture: A Finite Element Analysis Study
items.abstract: Ground vibrations induced by traffic and industrial activities can adversely affect human comfort and nearby sensitive equipment. Wave barriers, particularly open trenches (OTs), are recognized as effective vibration isolation solutions; however, their practical implementation may be limited by the difficulties associated with maintaining a fully OT. While trench infilling and sand crumb rubber mixture (SCRM) materials have been investigated separately, a continuous, non-alternating, partially SCRM-filled trench configuration has not yet been systematically evaluated through detailed numerical analysis for single and multiple trench arrangements. PLAXIS 2D was used to compare open, fully SCRM-filled, and partially SCRM-filled trenches at filling ratios of 25%, 50% and 75%, with the lower portion filled and the upper portion, within the near-surface zone of highest Rayleigh wave energy concentration, left open. Although the OT provided the highest isolation efficiency, followed by the 25% filling configuration, the 50% SCRM-filled configuration (SCRMT) emerged as a more practical alternative, achieving a barrier efficiency close to that of the OT (70% versus 75%, under identical conditions) while reducing the required unsupported open-trench depth by half and diverting waste tire material from landfills. The influence of trench depth, width, source-to-trench distance, and multiple-trench arrangement on SCRMT performance was also examined.
items.authors: Eda Arslan, Turgut Öztürk, Müge Balkaya

items.title: Floristic Composition and Structure Under Contrasting Soil Management Practices for Sustainable Vineyards in the Douro Demarcated Region
items.abstract: This study evaluated how contrasting vineyard soil management practices influence structural-floristic composition and its floristic quality in Mediterranean vineyard agroecosystems. Vegetation responses were assessed under mown sown cover crops (SOWN), mown spontaneous cover crops without soil amendment (SPONT), mown spontaneous cover crops after soil amendment application (AMEND), tillage (TILL), and herbicide application (HERB), and compared with surrounding spontaneous vegetation (SURROUND). Floristic and structural trajectories under different management regimes were also examined over time. HERB, TILL, SOWN, and AMEND showed greater divergence from the floristic and structural characteristics of SURROUND, whereas SPONT showed the highest floristic and structural variability and the greatest percentage of shared flora with SURROUND (36% of shared flora). The composition of the sown mixtures, including the introduction of allochthonous species in SOWN, and management practices, such as annual tillage, compost or biochar applications, and chemical control in the inter-row, were associated with a narrower range of floristic-structural configurations and, in some cases, with the presence of allochthonous flora. Temporal differences did not indicate a significant convergence towards the floristic-structural configuration of SPONT, suggesting that initial conditions and management history may influence vegetation development. Maintaining spontaneous vegetation may therefore retain floristic and structural characteristics more closely associated with SURROUND, providing an alternative approach for biodiversity-oriented vineyard management.
items.authors: Pedro Cardoso, Fátima Gonçalves, Cristina Carlos, António L. Crespí

items.title: Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification Leveraging Collaboration of Foundation Models
items.abstract: Foundation models have shown remarkable generalization ability for few-shot learning (FSL). However, their potential for remote sensing scene classification has not been fully explored. Existing methods mainly adapt a single vision–language model and seldom exploit the complementary strengths of different foundation models. Moreover, the inconsistency between visual and textual representations limits the effectiveness of cross-modal learning under limited supervision. To address these issues, we propose a framework for few-shot remote sensing scene classification leveraging collaboration of foundation models. Specifically, the proposed framework integrates a large language model, a text-to-image diffusion model, and a vision–language model to enrich class semantics, synthesize category-related training samples, and learn transferable visual-textual representations. Furthermore, a Deep Cross-modal Alignment (DCA) module is developed to improve feature consistency across modalities. The DCA module incorporates multi-scale visual features, lightweight adapters, and a contrastive learning objective to obtain more discriminative task-adaptive representations. Extensive experiments on 12 remote sensing scene classification datasets under various few-shot settings demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance compared with existing prompt learning and efficient parameter tuning methods, with consistent improvements observed on average across the evaluated datasets. Recent multimodal large language models evaluated in the zero-shot setting are additionally reported as references, while the 2-shot results of our method illustrate the performance when limited labeled data are available. This comparison provides a broader view of the trade-offs between label availability, classification accuracy, and inference cost across the two paradigms.
items.authors: Hong Ji, Zhi Gao, Yucheng Gong, Zhongyu Shi, Yuting Zhang, Xuesong Chai

items.title: Residents’ Perceptions of Importance and Satisfaction with Cultural and Creative Tourism Resources in a Rural Cross-Border Context
items.abstract: Cultural and creative tourism can support sustainable development in rural and cross-border areas by activating locally embedded cultural resources while strengthening community identity and destination distinctiveness. This study examines local residents’ perceptions of the importance of and satisfaction with cultural and creative attractions and activities in the rural cross-border municipalities of Matulji (Croatia) and Ilirska Bistrica (Slovenia). A quantitative field survey was conducted in March and April 2025 among 151 adult residents (Matulji: n = 99; Ilirska Bistrica: n = 52). Importance and satisfaction with the tourism valorisation of individual cultural and creative resources were measured on five-point Likert-type scales, and paired-samples t-tests were used to assess within-municipality differences between the two dimensions. The results show relatively high perceived importance of cultural and creative resources in both municipalities, but different patterns of alignment between importance and satisfaction. In Matulji, statistically significant gaps were identified for most of the assessed resources, whereas in Ilirska Bistrica, significant gaps were found for a smaller set of attractions and activities. Carnival customs combined high importance with high satisfaction in both local contexts, while several heritage, landscape and creative resources showed room for improved tourism valorisation. By applying a resource-specific importance–satisfaction perspective to residents in a rural cross-border setting, the study provides a more differentiated basis for identifying management priorities and for designing culturally sensitive, locally grounded tourism development.
items.authors: Romina Agbaba, Zrinka Zadel

items.title: Reticulocalbin-2 (RCN2) as a Context-Dependent CREC-Family Modulator: Gene Expression and Regulation, Molecular Biology, Disease Relevance, and Translational Challenges
items.abstract: Reticulocalbin-2 (RCN2), encoded by the human RCN2 gene (HGNC:9935) and historically identified as E6-binding protein, is a CREC-family EF-hand Ca2+-binding protein. Although first characterized as an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated protein, current evidence extends RCN2 biology to splice-variant and localization complexity, protein interactions, regulatory and signaling networks, extracellular activity, cancer, non-malignant disease, and the RCN2-derived hormone Raptin. This review synthesizes the fragmented and methodologically uneven RCN2 literature within an evidence-stratified framework. Mechanistic evidence, including direct biochemical assays and RCN2-directed functional studies, supports selected interaction and signaling relationships, whereas omics, database-derived and single-context observations remain hypothesis-generating. Across disease settings, RCN2 is best interpreted as a context-dependent modulator rather than a uniform oncogenic driver, validated biomarker or established therapeutic target. Translational progress will require molecular-form-specific assays, disease-specific validation and clinically grounded models.
items.authors: Abdullah A. A. Alghamdi

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Pyrolysis and Anaerobic Digestion as End-of-Life Options for Used Cork Stoppers
items.abstract: The cork industry generates valuable by-products and residues with significant potential within a circular bioeconomy framework. This study evaluated the energy-driven valorization of two post-consumer cork residues—natural cork stoppers (NCS) and technical cork stoppers (TCS)—through anaerobic digestion and pyrolysis. Both NCS and TCS exhibited low moisture and ash content, a high heating value of 25.14 and 29.88 MJ/kg, respectively, a carbon content exceeding 58 wt% and low nitrogen, sulfur and chlorine concentrations. These characteristics highlight the suitability of NCS and TCS for energy recovery applications. Anaerobic digestion produced biogas containing 68.5 vol% of methane after alkaline pretreatment of TCS. However, the maximum biochemical methane potential was low, reaching only 19.5 L CH4/kg VS. The resulting digestates contained nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium at levels compatible with agricultural use. Slow pyrolysis of the cork residues resulted in high biochar yields, with NCS achieving an average yield of 64.8 wt%. Combined with carbon contents of up to 66.3 wt%, the biochars produced from NCS and TCS show strong potential for valorization as solid energy carriers, as well as for applications such as activated carbon production and soil amendment. Overall, thermochemical conversion via pyrolysis proved to be the most effective pathway for energy valorization of the tested cork residues, whereas the performance of anaerobic digestion remained limited unless more intensive pretreatment strategies were applied.
items.authors: Patrícia Moura, João Jesus, Ana Eusébio, Paula Costa, Susana Marques, Ana Cristina Oliveira

items.title: Patient Journey and Treatment Patterns of Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer in Mexico
items.abstract: Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) accounts for most newly diagnosed bladder tumors, yet little is known about how it is managed in Mexico, particularly during prolonged Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) shortages. This retrospective, multicenter observational study characterized the clinical and histopathological profile, the diagnostic and treatment timelines, and the adherence to guideline-recommended care of patients with NMIBC treated at three tertiary referral hospitals in Mexico City. The records of 221 adults diagnosed between January 2010 and December 2020 were reviewed, and the risk of recurrence or progression was classified according to the European Association of Urology 2019 classification. The median age was 68 years (interquartile range [IQR] 59–75) and the male-to-female ratio was 3:1. Hematuria was the most frequent presenting symptom (83.3%). Three-quarters of patients had T1 tumors, 6.3% had concomitant carcinoma in situ, 84.6% had high-grade tumors, and 92.8% were at high risk of recurrence or progression. The median interval from symptom onset to histopathologic diagnosis was 167 days (IQR 81–329) and varied between centers. After diagnosis, the median time to second-look resection was 67 days (IQR 33.5–112) and to the first BCG instillation 92.5 days (IQR 41.8–165.5). Adjuvant intravesical therapy was administered to 66% of patients, most often BCG, although fewer than half of the BCG-treated patients (45%) completed induction, and 40% of the patients eligible for a second-look transurethral resection did not undergo it. Thirty percent of patients had no documented post-treatment surveillance. These real-world data provide a baseline description of NMIBC care in Mexican tertiary centers and identify specific, measurable gaps that may inform standardization and quality-improvement efforts in resource-constrained settings.
items.authors: Anna Scavuzzo, Ricardo Alonso Castillejos-Molina, Iván Bravo-Castro, Miguel A. Jiménez-Ríos, José G. Campos-Salcedo, Miguel A. Jiménez-Dávila

items.title: Bioaccumulative Response of Quercus robur L. to a Soil Sodification Gradient in a Central European Floodplain Forest
items.abstract: Under ongoing climate change and increasing land-use intensity, understanding the response of different tree species to soil sodification and salinization is essential for sustainable forest management. In this study, we evaluated the content of Na, Cl−, Fe, Mn, and SO42− in the leaves of 90 mature pedunculate oak (Quercus robur L.) trees growing in floodplain forests along a soil sodification gradient associated with shallow, highly mineralized groundwater. Foliar contents of Na+, Cl−, and SO42− showed no trend along the sodification gradient, whereas Mn and, to a lesser extent, Fe contents decreased with increasing sodification. All substances were only weakly related to soil predictors. Furthermore, coupling between soil and leaf contents was weak, indicating groundwater as the dominant influence. Despite decades of sodification, element contents remained substantially lower than values reported in experimental salinity studies on Quercus spp. and generally fell at the lower end of the range reported for salinization-affected sites. These findings suggest that mature Q. robur effectively regulate the physiological uptake and transport of salts into leaves, highlighting the species’ tolerance to long-term environmental sodification. The results support the suitability of Q. robur for environments affected by increasing soil salinization.
items.authors: David Juřička, Václav Pecina, Pavlína Kučerová, Valerie Vranová

items.title: A Two-Stage Prediction Strategy for Primary Hyperparathyroidism
items.abstract: Background: Primary hyperparathyroidism parathyroid hormone (PTH) hypersecretion is difficult to recognise when calcium is normal and difficult to distinguish from secondary hyperparathyroidism once PTH is found to be elevated. These are separate problems arising at separate points in care. We developed and evaluated two interpretable models corresponding to these decision points using an internal–external validation design. Methods: We analysed 2788 adults undergoing PTH testing across three campuses of one hospital (development n = 1843; internal–external validation n = 445 and n = 500); those with an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded. PHPT was adjudicated in 504 (18.1%) by two endocrinologists using biochemistry, imaging and histopathology. Model 1, for use before PTH is measured, comprised total calcium, ln(alkaline phosphatase) and age. Model 2, developed in the Main campus subgroup with PTH above the reference limit ( 65 pg/mL, n = 429 of 623), comprised ln(PTH), total calcium and phosphate. Results: Model 1 achieved AUCs of 0.920 in the development cohort and 0.882–0.908 in the validation cohorts; because serum calcium contributed to the outcome definition, these estimates reflect agreement with the reference standard rather than independent diagnostic accuracy. Among participants with elevated PTH, Model 2 achieved an AUC of 0.904 in the development cohort and 0.892 in the pooled validation cohort compared with 0.803 and 0.791 for PTH alone, respectively. In the normocalcaemic subgroup, Model 2 achieved an AUC of 0.790 compared with 0.699 for PTH alone. Applied sequentially, the models referred 18.0–26.1% of participants while capturing 78.1–85.0% of PHPT cases and identified a second-stage subgroup with an observed PHPT prevalence of 93.1–95.1%. Conclusions: This two-stage strategy may support further testing and referral for PHPT using routinely available measurements. Prospective validation in broader clinical populations is required before clinical implementation.
items.authors: Ruisi Chen, Min Ren, Jingyan Chen, Pin Wang

items.title: Mapping Digital Transformation Research in Women-Led SMEs: A Bibliometric Analysis and Resilience-Oriented Research Agenda
items.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face persistent pressure to convert digital transformation into organizational resilience amid continuous digital disruption. This capacity remains conceptually underdeveloped when digitalization and gender are treated as separate concerns. This study focuses on women-led SMEs because resilience mechanisms, including risk perception, digital self-efficacy, and access to institutional finance, are not gender neutral. This study maps the confluence of gender, SMEs, and digital transformation through a bibliometric analysis of 145 Web of Science publications (2016–2026). Resilience serves as the interpretive framework guiding this synthesis, informed by the bibliometric findings on gender, SMEs, and digital transformation. Co-occurrence, citation, and overlay networks, constructed using VOSviewer, examine temporal evolution, geographic distribution, and thematic structure. The field shows three periods of scholarly development, with 62.8% of output concentrated in 2023–2026. Keyword co-occurrence analysis, using a thesaurus file that consolidates conceptually related terms, shows that digital transformation’s connectivity is comparable to other central terms across every threshold tested. The literature’s limits lie in three more specific structural separations: between adoption vocabulary and firm-level strategy vocabulary, between digital transformation and institutional and financial vocabulary tied to unequal credit access, and in an almost complete absence of vocabulary for interorganizational collaboration; gender-specific barrier terminology is similarly absent from the dominant keyword vocabulary at every threshold tested. Citation network analysis reveals regional variation in citation impact, partly related to differences in publication recency across countries. The study proposes a six-area research agenda for SME managers, support organizations, and policymakers seeking to strengthen resilience through gender sensitive digital transformation.
items.authors: Adriana Tulbure, Anca Popescu, Nicoleta Andreea Neacșu

items.title: Antimicrobial Activity of Lipophilic Gallium-Based Compounds: An Emerging Frontier in Metal-Based Antimicrobials
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an increasing global health threat that underscores the urgent need for antimicrobial agents with mechanisms of action distinct from those of conventional antibiotics. Gallium (Ga) has emerged as a promising metal-based antimicrobial owing to the chemical similarity of Ga(III) to Fe(III), which enables it to interfere with bacterial iron acquisition and utilization. In contrast to Fe(III), Ga(III) is redox-inactive under physiological conditions and cannot support the redox reactions required for many iron-dependent cellular processes, thereby disrupting bacterial metabolism. This review highlights recent advances in gallium-based antimicrobial strategies, with particular emphasis on the role of ligand coordination in modulating the antibacterial activity of Ga(III) against drug-resistant pathogens. Emerging evidence indicates that coordination with lipophilic ligands can enhance the cellular update and accumulation of Ga(III) and may confer additional antibacterial effects beyond Fe(III) mimicry alone. These findings suggest that ligand design is a key strategy for tuning the physicochemical properties and antimicrobial activity of gallium complexes. Rational development of ligand-coordinated Ga(III) complexes may therefore provide new therapeutic approaches for combating multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.
items.authors: Nalin Abeydeera, Bishnu Pant, Guanyu Chen

items.title: VERITAS: A Multilingual Temporal and Conflict-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework
items.abstract: Most benchmarks used to evaluate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems assume a static world: they say little about how well a system handles new information, conflicting evidence, multiple languages, or questions that simply cannot be answered from the available evidence. This study introduces VERITAS, an adaptive, temporal- and conflict-aware RAG pipeline built to improve multilingual answer quality without sacrificing source grounding. It combines need-based update routing, hybrid BM25/dense retrieval, cross-lingual evidence access, multilingual reranking, temporal and source-trust ranking, conflict verification, history-aware filtering, adaptive context construction, and citation verification, all built around a single frozen Qwen3-8B generator shared across every method compared. To evaluate it, we built Adaptive Knowledge v6, a 3,000-item benchmark spanning Kazakh, Russian, and English across five knowledge conditions: stable, new, updated, conflicting, and unanswerable. On a deterministic 999-item test split, VERITAS reached 60.06% accuracy and 74.02% token F1, against 52.95% and 70.62% for the strongest baseline, a statistically significant +7.11 percentage-point gain (95% paired-bootstrap CI [4.40, 9.71]; McNemar p = 2.22 × 10⁻⁷). The improvement was largest on conflicting and unanswerable items but did not carry over uniformly to updated knowledge. VERITAS also showed a coverage–grounding trade-off, with accepted-answer coverage of 70.67%. Together, these results point to real gains under heterogeneous knowledge conditions, while also surfacing wrong abstention and updated-knowledge handling as the clearest targets for future work.
items.authors: Alibek Orynbek, Kainizhamal Iklassova, Azamat Serek

items.title: Oregano Essential Oil Alleviates Diquat-Induced Oxidative Stress in Calves and Modulates Rumen Microbiota
items.abstract: Oxidative stress can impair calf health and performance, and oregano essential oil (OEO) has potential antioxidant activity. This study evaluated dietary OEO in a diquat-induced oxidative-stress model using 24 weaned male Holstein calves assigned to a 2 × 2 factorial design with OEO supplementation (0 or 8 g/day) and diquat challenge (saline or 8 mg/kg body weight). Growth performance, serum biochemical, antioxidant, oxidative-damage and inflammatory indices, hepatic Nrf2-related antioxidant gene expression, rumen microbiota, and rumen metabolomics were assessed. The results showed that growth responses were phase dependent: OEO increased overall average daily gain (ADG) and dry matter intake (DMI), whereas diquat reduced overall ADG; no OEO × diquat interaction was detected for overall growth outcomes. The OEO group had higher serum SOD, GSH-Px, and T-AOC levels and lower levels of selected oxidative-damage and inflammatory indices, although the responses varied by endpoint and time point. Hepatic RT-qPCR showed treatment-associated differences in Keap1, HMOX1, GCLC, GCLM, and SOD1 expression. Rumen 16S rRNA gene sequencing showed treatment-associated shifts in microbial community composition, whereas PICRUSt2 predicted differences in microbial functional potential, including amino-acid-metabolism-related functions. Untargeted metabolomics identified treatment-associated differences in rumen metabolite profiles and KEGG pathway-enrichment patterns. Correlation analysis indicated that OEO-associated characteristic metabolites were positively correlated with antioxidant markers and negatively correlated with oxidative-damage and pro-inflammatory indices. Overall, OEO supplementation was associated with improved antioxidant status and distinct rumen microbial-metabolic profiles in diquat-challenged calves, supporting its potential as a natural feed additive, while the involvement of specific molecular pathways requires further validation.
items.authors: Meixian Zhang, Huan Chen, Ting Liu, Yunbo Wang, Yining Cheng, Yingquan Hao

items.title: Emotions Toward the Institution of the Church: Development of a New Measure
items.abstract: The aim of the study was to develop a scale for measuring emotions toward the Church as an institution. In Study 1, the initial development of the Emotions Toward the Church Scale (ETC) involved compiling a list of 91 Church-related emotions. Following evaluation by expert judges, the list was reduced to 27 items, which were administered to a representative sample of Polish adults (N = 518). Based on the results of an exploratory factor analysis, two factors were identified—positive emotions toward the Church and negative emotions toward the Church—and the final 24-item version of the ETC was established. In Study 2, also conducted on a nationwide sample of Polish adults (N = 1943), confirmatory factor analysis provided support for the two-factor structure identified in Study 1, with overall model fit indices indicating a moderate fit. The ETC demonstrated high internal consistency (α = 0.95 for positive emotions toward the Church and α = 0.96 for negative emotions toward the Church). The scale may serve as a valuable tool for examining perceptions of institutional forms of religion and the affective experiences associated with them.
items.authors: Anna Tychmanowicz, Barbara Gawda, Beata Zarzycka, Anna Błaszczak, Natalia Jach-Salamon, Karolina Ludwikowska-Świeboda

items.title: Mobility and Logistics as a Service for Healthcare (MLaaS4H): Transport Planning Processes for Enhancing Sustainable People Mobility to Healthcare Facilities
items.abstract: Rapid urbanisation poses increasingly complex sustainability challenges, while transport systems remain essential for enabling people and businesses to conduct daily activities and access critical services. This study investigates the interactions between passenger and freight mobility and the healthcare sector and proposes Mobility and Logistics as a Service for Healthcare (MLaaS4H), an integrated framework for the sustainable planning of healthcare-related mobility and logistics. The framework aims to support decision-making and service design by combining advanced transport system models (TSMs) with emerging information and communication technologies (e-ICTs), thereby improving accessibility to healthcare facilities and the efficiency of service provision. The proposed planning process comprises two complementary paths. The external path connects the spatial, temporal, and deepening dimensions of transport and healthcare planning, whereas the internal path adopts the Logical Framework Approach (LFA) to establish a transparent causal chain linking invested resources, implemented activities, outputs, outcomes, and long-term goals. Indicators associated with each component are connected through exogenous and endogenous functions, enabling quantitative assessment of the efficiency and effectiveness of MLaaS4H solutions. An illustrative case study demonstrates how coordinated healthcare appointments, public transport services, integrated digital platforms, and rebooking mechanisms can increase access opportunities, reduce temporal mismatches, support vulnerable users, and mitigate private vehicle dependence. While the example addresses passenger mobility, TSMs are equally applicable to freight transport and logistics activities. The proposed framework provides a structured basis for ex ante evaluation and coordinated planning and is intended for researchers in the healthcare and mobility fields, as well as practitioners involved in decision-making and implementation processes.
items.authors: Corrado Rindone

items.title: From Algorithmic Detection to Adaptive Fisheries Governance: An AI-Enabled Compliance and Ecosystem Feedback Framework for IUU Fishing in the Yellow Sea
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly able to infer apparent fishing activity, vessel type, encounters, non-cooperative or otherwise low-visibility vessel presence, and other maritime patterns from Automatic Identification System (AIS), vessel monitoring system (VMS), radar, optical imagery and catch records. Yet better detection does not automatically produce better fisheries management. This article asks under what institutional conditions AI-enabled monitoring can support more effective compliance and the sustainability of shared fish stocks without converting probabilistic signals into automatic enforcement findings. Using the Korea–China Yellow Sea as an institutional case study, the analysis combines recent AI-fisheries literature, international monitoring–control–surveillance guidance, ecosystem-based fisheries scholarship, the Korea–China Fisheries Agreement and verifiable official enforcement and resource-management developments through August 2026. It develops an Adaptive Fisheries Intelligence Loop (AFIL) with five stages: observe, validate, respond, learn and adapt. The model requires human validation of algorithmic signals, provenance labels for shared information, feedback from enforcement outcomes, and a second feedback channel connecting compliance patterns to ecological indicators and management measures. Applied to the Yellow Sea, AFIL supports joint risk vocabularies, interoperable case and vessel histories, targeted patrols, scientific stock assessment and periodic recalibration of both algorithms and management rules. AFIL is an institutionally plausible and testable governance design, not an empirically validated prediction that AI will itself deliver compliance. The article therefore argues that AI should be governed as adaptive decision-support infrastructure rather than as an automated enforcement endpoint.
items.authors: Wanwoo Nam

items.title: Podiatric Hospitalist: Better Care Model
items.abstract: A multidisciplinary team approach has become essential to modern hospital care, bringing together professionals from different specialties to collaborate on patient management. A Podiatric Hospitalist (PH) is a board-eligible or board-certified Doctor of Podiatric Medicine dedicated to the evaluation and management of acutely hospitalized patients with foot and ankle conditions. PHs play a vital role in this collaborative model, particularly in managing different conditions affecting the foot, ankle, and the lower extremities. Beyond serving as the gatekeepers for prevention and management of diabetic foot ulcers, PHs facilitate high-quality and efficient management of diverse lower extremity disorders including infection, trauma, sport-related injuries and chronic conditions related to diabetes, peripheral arterial disease, and autoimmune disorders. We present a care model, informed by our institutional experience, that positions the PH as a consultative and co-management member of a multidisciplinary foot and ankle and limb-salvage team, with the goal of advancing high-value care that improves outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and patient satisfaction. By integrating specialized lower extremity expertise into collaborative patient management, PHs help improve patient outcomes, enhance coordination of care, and support both preventative and surgical management strategies across multiple clinical settings. This collaborative approach enhances the quality and efficiency of healthcare delivery in hospitals. As the demand for limb salvage and high-value inpatient care continues to grow, the PH represents a practical and timely addition to multidisciplinary foot and ankle care.
items.authors: Mentor Thaqi, Enrico Prajiante Bertolino, Pavel Kibrik, Jeffrey Shook, Lee Kirksey
items.category_raw: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association

items.title: Beyond Direct Touch: Passive Canine Presence Is Associated with Lower Anxiety in South American University Students
items.abstract: University students are experiencing increasing levels of anxiety, attracting interest in accessible strategies that support wellbeing within educational settings. Animal-assisted interventions have shown beneficial effects on stress and anxiety in students. However, most studies have focused on direct and active interactions with dogs rather than their passive presence. This quasi-experimental study evaluated whether the presence of a dog during regular classroom activities was associated with reduced anxiety among university students. A total of 127 undergraduate students from Veterinary Medicine and Law programs at a Chilean university participated in a repeated-measures pretest–posttest design. State and trait anxiety were assessed before and after class using the Spanish version of the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI). Students attending classes with a dog present reported significantly lower state anxiety (0.300 ± 0.116 vs. 0.384 ± 0.139; p 0.001) and trait anxiety (0.257 ± 0.140 vs. 0.352 ± 0.155; p 0.001) than students in control classrooms (no dog present). Mixed-design repeated-measures ANOVAs revealed significant Time × Exposure interactions for both State Anxiety and Trait Anxiety, indicating different temporal anxiety trajectories between exposed and control students. These findings suggest that the passive presence of a trained dog may contribute to lower anxiety levels in university students and could represent a simple, feasible and low-resource wellbeing strategy, particularly relevant for higher education institutions in the context of Latin America and other Global South regions.
items.authors: Maximiliano Cavieres, Ana María Urrutia, Gonzalo Chavez, Hernan Cañon-Jones

items.title: N-Acetylcysteine in Schizophrenia: A Convergent Redox-Based Approach to Therapeutic Potential
items.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) remains one of the most disabling psychiatric disorders, in large part because current antipsychotics (APs) inadequately address negative symptoms and cognitive deficits. Converging evidence implicates a set of interconnected mechanisms, NMDAR hypofunction, oxidative stress, and a possible low-grade neuroimmune activation, that converge on parvalbumin-positive GABAergic interneuron dysfunction, the likely substrate of these refractory symptom domains. N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) is an adjunctive candidate because it may act on several of these pathways: it replenishes glutathione (GSH), restores redox balance, and modulates glutamatergic transmission, while its immunomodulatory effects remain poorly characterized in SCZ. This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence from preclinical models and clinical trials, showing that NAC produces replicated but modest benefits for negative symptoms and cognitive function, with inconsistent effects on positive symptoms. Notably, null findings in clinical-high-risk and treatment-resistant populations, together with a single exploratory subgroup analysis in early psychosis in which a peripheral redox index (erythrocyte glutathione peroxidase activity) was associated with positive-symptom response, raise the hypothesis that NAC efficacy may depend on a pre-existing, measurable antioxidant deficit. Adequately powered, biomarker-enriched trials that stratify patients by redox status are therefore needed to determine whether NAC is an effective targeted therapy for a mechanistically defined SCZ subgroup. Such trials would resolve whether the modest effect sizes observed in unselected populations reflect true but limited efficacy or dilution by enrolment of redox-normal patients unlikely to benefit.
